about: The direct step's live run of the design example '03-salt-ice' (20 Oct 2026): Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) through the gateway, measured by the engine's executor (web/export/shots.js checkPlan). Each round: the plan the model answered, and what the executor's checks said of it.

lesson.question: Is this a valid experiment to test salt?
lesson.answer: Valid. Both cubes are on plates, so the plates are the same. Only the salt is different.
words: Now the cubes sit on white plates.

payload.concept: a fair test changes only one thing: salt on one ice cube

plan.title: Is it a fair test? Salt on one ice cube
plan.about: Two equal ice cubes sit on two equal white plates, and only one has salt on it, so the test changes just one thing: the salt.

source.question: Is this a valid experiment to test salt?
source.answer: Valid. Both cubes are on plates, so the plates are the same. Only the salt is different.
words: Now the cubes sit on white plates.

story.says: Two ice cubes, each on its own white plate.
The left cube has a little pile of salt on top.
The right cube is the same, but it has no salt.
Same cubes, same plates: only the salt is different.

shots.intent: Open on the whole setup before anything happens: two ice cubes, each on a white plate, seen a little from above so the plates and the cube tops show.

audit.question: Can a child see two ice cubes, each sitting on its own white plate?

shots.intent: Cut in close on the left cube so the small white pile of salt on its top is big and easy to see: this is the one thing being tested.

audit.question: Can a child see a little pile of salt sitting on top of the left ice cube?

shots.intent: The same close look at the right cube, at the same size and angle, so the child sees it is the same kind of cube but with a bare top: no salt.

audit.question: Can a child see that the right ice cube has nothing on top of it?

shots.intent: For the question, put the two cubes side by side, one column each at one scale, each on its whole plate: same cubes, same plates, salt on one only, labelled. Hold still so the child can compare.

audit.question: Can a Grade 3 child see two same ice cubes on two same white plates, with salt on only one cube?

plan.notes: The lesson pauses at the setup, so every shot freezes pause:setup (t=0): the salt dissolves by 0.2 s and the cubes melt in the time-lapse afterwards, so none of the run's motion is shown. The two plates stand 0.37 m apart, so the pause uses split columns at one scale (0.24 m per band) instead of one wide picture where the salt would be too small. The salt is in the left lane's cast only and is named by its item id.
